claims.text: Optimistic concurrency takes no locks; it makes the data modification fail on save if the data changed since it was queried, and the failure is reported to the application.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Handling Concurrency Conflicts, 'Optimistic concurrency'

claims.text: xmin is a system column present on every PostgreSQL row (the id of the transaction that wrote that row version); an UPDATE creates a new row version with a new xmin.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs 5.6 System Columns (xmin); 13.1 MVCC introduction

claims.text: With the Npgsql EF Core provider, IsRowVersion() on a uint property maps it to PostgreSQL's xmin system column and makes it a concurrency token.
claims.source_hint: Npgsql EF Core docs: Concurrency Tokens (xmin, IsRowVersion); DonHangDbContext.cs:61-65 @ stage-2

claims.text: A concurrency token's value is loaded and tracked with the entity; on UPDATE, EF Core adds a condition on the token's original value to the WHERE clause.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Handling Concurrency Conflicts (UPDATE ... WHERE [PersonId] = @p1 AND [Version] = @p2)

claims.text: When the guarded UPDATE affects zero rows instead of the expected one, SaveChanges throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Handling Concurrency Conflicts

claims.text: Under Read Committed the waiting UPDATE re-evaluates its WHERE on the updated row version after the lock holder commits; with the new xmin the condition fails and the row is not updated.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs 13.2.1 Read Committed (re-evaluates WHERE on updated version); concurrency-conflict.sh comment @ stage-2

claims.text: When SaveChanges fails, the transaction it started rolls back and none of its changes apply, so the notification row the cancel's save adds (notifier.Send before SaveChangesAsync) is not written either.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Transactions, Default transaction behavior; OrderService.cs:40-49 @ stage-2 (notifier.Send before SaveChangesAsync)

claims.text: Inside one transaction under Read Committed, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks the rows it returns; a second transaction trying to lock them waits until the first ends, then gets the updated row and reads the committed status.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs: SELECT, The Locking Clause; 13.3.2 Row-Level Locks

claims.text: When many writers compete for one row, waiting in line can cost less than failing and reloading repeatedly; with rare conflicts the token adds little: one more WHERE condition, and a failure's cost only when one happens.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Handling Concurrency Conflicts ('assumes that concurrency conflicts are relatively rare'; pessimistic approaches lock up-front)

claims.text: Order.Version is a uint with a private setter; the AddOrderVersionToken migration writes no SQL with the Npgsql provider because xmin already exists, so orders gets no new column.

ExceptionHandlingMiddleware catches DbUpdateConcurrencyException and answers 409 with title 'Order was changed by another request', detail 'reload the order and try again', type .../concurrent-update and orderId from ex.Entries.

Under Repeatable Read, an UPDATE of a row that a concurrent transaction changed and committed makes the transaction fail with a serialization error, SQLSTATE 40001, and the whole transaction must be retried from the beginning.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs 13.2.2 Repeatable Read Isolation Level; 13.4 Serialization Failure Handling

claims.text: Calling SaveChangesAsync again without refreshing sends the same UPDATE with the same original token, matching no row again; overwriting the token's original value with the database's current one and saving makes the save succeed.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs: Handling Concurrency Conflicts, Resolving concurrency conflicts (original values must be refreshed)

claims.text: concurrency-conflict.sh ships order 5 in a psql session holding the row ~2 s, cancels via the API meanwhile: the API answers 409 with type .../concurrent-update and orderId 5, the ship shows UPDATE 1 and COMMIT, order 5 ends shipped, then reset to paid.
